_about: Inside every part: the kits a part can open when you zoom in. Each slot has options; the first option is the default. Effects: massF/costF multiply the part's dry mass and cost, massD/costD add kg and $, rel adds to reliability, isp adds seconds (engines and solid motors), thrustF multiplies thrust, powerF multiplies power, chuteF multiplies parachute drag.

slots.name: Turbopump cycle
slots.role: How the pump that feeds the chamber is driven.

options.name: Gas generator
options.note: A small burner spins the turbine, then its exhaust is dumped overboard. Merlin, Vulcain, F-1.
cons: Throws away 2–3 % of the propellant unburned

options.name: Staged combustion
options.note: The turbine exhaust goes into the main chamber, so nothing is wasted. Higher pressure, higher Isp, far harder to build.

options.name: Expander
options.note: Hydrogen heated in the chamber walls spins the turbine. Gentle and endlessly restartable, but only enough power for a small engine.
cons: Thrust −15 %: the cycle cannot drive a big pump

options.name: Electric pump
options.note: Battery-driven motors spin the pumps. The simplest plumbing there is; the batteries are heavy.

options.name: Pressure-fed (no pump)
options.note: No pump at all: tank pressure pushes propellant into the chamber. Unlimited restarts, but the thick tanks and low pressure cost thrust and Isp.
options.real: AJ10 (Delta II second stage), Apollo SPS

slots.name: Injector
slots.role: The plate that sprays fuel and oxidizer into the chamber.

options.name: Coaxial swirl
options.note: Hundreds of small elements, oxidizer inside, fuel swirling around it. Smooth combustion.

options.name: Pintle
options.note: One central element: a pin with a sleeve. Deep throttling, cheap to make, hard to make unstable.

options.name: Impinging jets
options.note: Jets of fuel and oxidizer collide and mix. Simple; prone to rough combustion.

slots.name: Nozzle extension
slots.role: The lower skirt of the bell and how it is kept from melting.

options.name: Regeneratively cooled
options.note: Fuel runs through channels in the bell wall before it burns, keeping the metal cool and preheating the fuel.
pros: Runs as long as there is fuel

options.name: Radiatively cooled niobium
options.note: A thin skirt of C-103 niobium that simply glows orange and radiates the heat away. Light; only for vacuum.

options.name: Carbon-carbon skirt
options.note: Woven carbon fibre in a carbon matrix: half the mass of metal and happy at 2,000 °C.
pros: +4 s of Isp from a longer bell

options.name: Extendable nozzle
options.note: A second skirt that slides down after staging, so a huge bell fits in a short interstage.
cons: One more mechanism that must work

slots.name: Igniter
slots.role: How the engine is lit, and how many times.

options.name: Spark torch
options.note: A small spark-lit torch in the chamber wall. Restartable as long as there is power.
cons: Needs power and a pilot flow

options.name: Pyrotechnic
options.note: A one-shot cartridge. The simplest igniter; one start only.

options.name: TEA-TEB slugs
options.note: Chemicals that burst into green flame on contact with oxygen. Reliable relights, limited by how many slugs you carry.

slots.name: Bulkhead between fuel and oxidizer
slots.role: How the two propellants are kept apart.

options.name: Separate domes
options.note: Two tanks, two domes, a short section between them. Simple and safe.
cons: Heavier: two domes and a gap

options.name: Common bulkhead
options.note: One insulated wall shared by both propellants. Saves a dome and a metre of skin; the hardest thing to build in the tank.
cons: A leak mixes fuel and oxidizer

slots.name: Pressurisation
slots.role: What fills the space as propellant drains.

options.name: Helium bottles inside
options.note: Cold helium bottles sit inside the oxygen tank, where they stay dense. Proven; the bottles are a hazard.

options.name: Autogenous (hot propellant gas)
options.note: A little propellant is heated by the engine and piped back as gas. No helium at all.
pros: No helium to run out of
cons: Only works once the engine runs

slots.name: Slosh baffles
slots.role: Rings inside the tank that stop the propellant sloshing.

options.name: Ring baffles
options.note: Rings welded inside the wall break up the waves when the ship turns.

options.name: No baffles
options.note: Save the mass and hope. Sloshing propellant knocked Falcon 1 flight 2 into a spin.

slots.name: Insulation
slots.role: What keeps cold propellant from boiling off.

options.name: Bare metal
options.note: Fine for kerosene; cryogenic propellant boils off in the hours on the pad.

options.name: Spray-on foam
options.note: The orange foam of the Shuttle tank. Keeps hydrogen and oxygen liquid for hours; a piece of it struck Columbia.

options.name: Multilayer blankets
options.note: Gold foil layers for the long cruise: the only insulation that works in vacuum for weeks.

slots.name: Feed lines
slots.role: The pipes that carry propellant from the tank to the engine.

options.name: Single feed line
options.note: One big pipe per propellant.
cons: One valve failure stops the engine

options.name: Redundant feed lines
options.note: Two pipes and two valves per propellant, so one can fail.

slots.name: Flight computer
slots.role: The computer that flies the ship and how many copies of it there are.

options.name: Single computer
options.note: One flight computer. If it fails, the crew flies by hand.

options.name: Triple redundant, voting
options.note: Three computers vote on every command; one can fail without anyone noticing.

options.name: Four plus a backup
options.note: Four identical computers and a fifth with different software, as the Shuttle flew.

slots.name: Life-support loop
slots.role: Air and water: used once, or recycled.

options.name: Open loop
options.note: Oxygen from tanks, CO₂ into canisters, water from bags. Simple; it lasts as long as the stores do.

options.name: Regenerative loop
options.note: Water split into oxygen, CO₂ scrubbed and recycled, like the station. Heavy, but it runs for months.

slots.name: Crew couches
slots.role: What the crew sits in through launch and landing.

options.name: Fixed couches
options.note: Padded seats bolted to the floor.
cons: A hard landing is felt in full

options.name: Shock-attenuating couches
options.note: Seats hung on crushable struts that soak up a hard landing.

slots.name: Windows
slots.role: How much of the wall is glass.

options.name: Small ports
options.note: Two small panes of fused silica. Strong wall, little view.

options.name: Panoramic windows
options.note: Big triple-pane windows. The view of a lifetime, and a weaker, heavier wall.

slots.name: Hatch
slots.role: Which way the door opens.

options.name: Outward, quick release
options.note: Opens outward in seconds, even against cabin pressure. The rule since 1967.

options.name: Inward plug hatch
options.note: Cabin pressure seals it tighter. It cannot be opened against that pressure: the Apollo 1 crew died behind one.
cons: Cannot open in a cabin fire

slots.name: Flight computer
slots.role: The launcher's guidance computer.

options.name: Dual string
options.note: Two computers, each able to fly alone.

options.name: Triple voting
options.note: Three computers vote.

slots.name: Inertial measurement unit
slots.role: The gyroscopes and accelerometers that sense every turn and push.

options.name: Ring-laser gyros
options.note: Light beams racing around a triangle of mirrors. The launcher standard.

options.name: Fibre-optic gyros
options.note: The same trick in a coil of fibre: lighter, no moving parts.

options.name: MEMS chips
options.note: Phone-grade silicon gyros, a hundred of them averaged.

slots.name: Telemetry & range safety
slots.role: The radios that report home and listen for the destruct command.

options.name: Single transmitter
options.note: One S-band transmitter and one command receiver.
cons: One failure and the range loses the vehicle

options.name: Dual, cross-strapped
options.note: Two of everything, either able to serve the whole ring.

slots.name: Propellant grain
slots.role: The shape of the hole cast through the propellant, which sets the thrust curve.

options.name: Star grain
options.note: A star-shaped bore gives steady thrust the whole burn.

options.name: High-thrust grain
options.note: More burning surface: +15 % thrust, a shorter burn, slightly less Isp.

options.name: Long-burn grain
options.note: Less surface, a long gentle burn: −15 % thrust, +3 s Isp.

slots.name: Nozzle
slots.role: Fixed, or swivelling to steer.

options.name: Fixed nozzle
options.note: Bolted straight. The core engine steers.

options.name: Vectoring nozzle
options.note: A flexible seal lets the nozzle swing a few degrees. Needed when the solids give most of the thrust.

slots.name: Separation
slots.role: How the fairing comes apart once the air is thin.

options.name: Two halves (bisector)
options.note: The fairing splits down the middle and the halves swing away on hinges.

options.name: Three petals
options.note: Three lighter pieces, each needing its own pushers.

slots.name: Acoustic blankets
slots.role: Padding against the roar of liftoff, which can shake a payload apart.

options.name: None
options.note: Bare composite skin. Loud inside: 140 dB at liftoff.

options.name: Acoustic blankets
options.note: Foam and fibre panels that cut the sound by 10 dB.

slots.name: Release
slots.role: What throws the pieces clear.

options.name: Pyrotechnic
options.note: Explosive bolts and a shaped cord. Sudden and loud.

options.name: Pneumatic pushers
options.note: Gas pistons shove the halves away gently.

slots.name: Ablator thickness
slots.role: How much material there is to burn away.

options.name: Standard
options.note: Sized for one entry with margin.

options.name: Thick
options.note: A quarter more ablator for a steep or hot entry.

slots.name: Seams
slots.role: How the blocks of shield are joined.

options.name: Gap filler
options.note: Blocks of ablator with a soft filler between them.
cons: Fillers can protrude and trip the flow

options.name: One piece
options.note: The whole shield cast as one block. No seams, hard to make.

slots.name: Shock absorber
slots.role: What soaks up the touchdown.

options.name: Crushable honeycomb
options.note: Aluminium honeycomb that crushes once. Light and certain.

options.name: Hydraulic struts
options.note: Oil and gas struts that reset. Heavier; reusable.

slots.name: Foot pads
slots.role: How big the feet are.

options.name: Small pads
options.note: Fine on rock.

options.name: Large pads
options.note: Snowshoes for dust.

slots.name: Solar cells
slots.role: Which kind of cell covers the panel.

options.name: Silicon
options.note: 20 % efficient. Cheap and tough.

options.name: Triple-junction GaAs
options.note: Three layers, each catching a different colour: 30 %+ efficient.

slots.name: Array drive
slots.role: Whether the panel turns to follow the Sun.

options.name: Fixed
options.note: Bolted to the hull. Power depends on where the ship points.

options.name: Sun-tracking drive
options.note: A motor and slip rings keep the panel facing the Sun.
cons: A motor that must not jam

slots.name: Canopy
slots.role: The shape of the chute.

options.name: Disk-gap-band
options.note: The Mars standard: a disk, a gap, a band. Opens supersonic without tearing.

options.name: Ringsail
options.note: Rings of sail cloth: more drag per kilogram, subsonic only.

slots.name: Reefing
slots.role: Whether the chute opens in stages.

options.name: Full open
options.note: One hard jerk.
cons: Peak load tears a weak chute

options.name: Staged reefing
options.note: Cutters release the canopy in two steps, halving the peak load.
